name: Atacama Desert (Yungay)
note: The driest non-polar desert on Earth. Used for Mars soil and life-detection drilling tests (NASA ARADS).

name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island
note: A 23 km impact crater in polar desert with permafrost. Home of the NASA Haughton-Mars Project.

name: Death Valley
note: Salt pans, alluvial fans and the Ubehebe volcanic craters. A long-running test area for Mars rovers and instruments.

name: Hanksville (MDRS)
note: The Mars Society's Mars Desert Research Station, set among red mudstones and sandstones.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
note: Among the coldest and driest ice-free land on Earth. A classic analog for Martian permafrost and polygons.

name: Holuhraun & Askja
note: A fresh 2014–15 basalt lava field next to Askja, where Apollo astronauts trained in geology.

name: Mauna Kea / Mauna Loa
note: Basaltic tephra and lava tubes. Site of the HI-SEAS habitat and lunar regolith and resource-extraction tests.

name: Lanzarote
note: Volcanic fields and long lava tubes. Used for ESA's PANGAEA astronaut geology training.

name: Río Tinto
note: An acidic, iron- and sulfate-rich river whose minerals (jarosite, hematite) resemble Meridiani Planum.

name: Bockfjorden
note: Volcanic and carbonate rocks in permafrost. The AMASE expeditions tested Mars rover instruments here.

name: Meteor Crater
note: A 1.2 km, well-preserved impact crater used to train Apollo astronauts.

name: Craters of the Moon
note: Basalt lava flows and lava tubes. A NASA field site for volcanic and cave studies.

name: Mistastin Lake crater
note: One of few impact craters in anorthosite, the main rock of the lunar highlands. Used for some lunar field studies, but heavily vegetated.

name: Allan Hills blue ice
note: Wind-scoured blue ice that concentrates meteorites, including the Mars meteorite ALH84001. Extreme, steady cold.

name: Dallol, Danakil Depression
note: Acidic, hypersaline hot springs on salt flats below sea level. Studied for the limits of life and for Mars-like sulfate and iron chemistry.

name: Qaidam Basin (Lenghu)
note: A high, cold, hyper-arid basin with salt crusts and large wind-carved ridges (yardangs).

name: Puna de Atacama (Antofalla)
note: A plateau near 4,000 m with thin air, very high UV, salt flats and young volcanoes. Known to microbiologists, rarely used for mission tests.

name: Kamil Crater
note: A 45 m impact crater first spotted on satellite images in 2008, with its ejecta and iron-meteorite fragments still intact in hyper-arid desert.

name: Gilf Kebir Plateau
note: A remote sandstone plateau cut by dry valleys, with steep scarps and wind-polished surfaces. Rarely surveyed as a planetary analog.

name: White Desert (Farafra)
note: Chalk towers and yardangs carved by wind. Its carbonate bedrock is relevant to the carbonates Perseverance is studying at Jezero.

name: Great Sand Sea
note: Long linear mega-dunes in a sand sea. An analog for Martian dune fields and wind-driven sand transport.

name: Dasht-e Lut
note: Satellites have measured ground temperatures near 70 °C here. Giant yardangs in old lake sediments look like Martian wind-eroded terrain.

name: Harrat Khaybar
note: A young basaltic lava field with lava tubes such as Umm Jirsan, and almost no vegetation.

name: Bayuda Volcanic Field
note: A dense field of cinder cones and maars on basalt plains in hyper-arid desert. Comparable in rock type to the lunar maria.

name: Emi Koussi, Tibesti
note: A large shield volcano with summit calderas rising above the Sahara. Its shape has been compared with Martian volcanoes such as Elysium Mons.

name: Wabar craters
note: Small impact craters among the dunes of the Empty Quarter, with impact glass and iron-meteorite fragments.

name: Fiskenæsset anorthosite
note: One of Earth's oldest anorthosite complexes, about 2.97 billion years old, beside the ice sheet. A cold stand-in for lunar highland rock.

name: Plateau east of Kharga Oasis
note: Best-scoring area in the Egypt scan for Jezero (86% in Earth Engine). Bare Eocene limestone plateau above the eastern Kharga escarpment: no measurable rain, flat to gently sloping. Part of a 3,000 km² belt of top-0.5% pixels around Kharga. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Abu Tartur Plateau (north)
note: Limestone plateau between Dakhla and Kharga, about 500 m high, also known for Egypt's largest phosphate deposit. Scored 85% for Jezero; rock-type guess from ASTER: carbonate. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Limestone plateau between Kharga and Edfu
note: The largest single candidate area (about 790 km²): a flat, bare limestone surface between Kharga Oasis and the Nile. Scored 84% for Jezero. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Plateau north of Dakhla Oasis
note: A separate cluster of about 1,000 km² of top-scoring pixels on the plateau north of Dakhla. ASTER suggests a mix of carbonate and salt/sulfate-like surfaces. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Sinn el-Kaddab Plateau near Kurkur
note: Limestone plateau around Kurkur Oasis, about 60 km west of Aswan, with relict spring-fed carbonate (tufa) deposits. Scored 84% for Jezero; fossil spring carbonates are an interesting parallel to Jezero's lake carbonates. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Eastern Desert east of Lake Nasser
note: A 520 km² candidate area east of the northern end of Lake Nasser. Scored 84% for Jezero; rock-type guess: carbonate. Found by the Earth Engine scan; check it in satellite imagery before using it.

name: Atacama coast range (Tarapacá)
note: Highest single 5 km pixel in the world scan for Jezero (84%). Hyper-arid coastal range of the Atacama, north of the studied Yungay site. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Salt deposits (evaporite) from ASTER. NASA EMIT (159 detections) finds no gypsum, and halite is invisible to it, so evaporite is kept.

name: Aksai Chin plateau
note: Centre of the largest top-0.5% area for Jezero in the world scan: a cold, high, dry plateau with salt lakes. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Carbonate from ASTER, confirmed by NASA EMIT: carbonate in 56% of 50 mineral detections.

name: Qiangtang (Changtang) plateau
note: Highest Arcadia score outside Antarctica in the world scan. Continuous, ice-rich permafrost at high altitude; we found no study matching it to Arcadia's buried ice. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 55% of 62 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Victoria Island
note: Largest top-0.5% area for Arcadia outside Antarctica: flat, cold polar lowland with permafrost. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Al Haruj volcanic field
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar pit. A 45,000 km² field of fluid (pāhoehoe-type) basalt with inflation tumuli, the lava type that forms tubes; no lava tubes documented in our search. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type: Al Haruj is basalt (published geology); NASA EMIT cannot see basalt minerals, and the clay it detects is dust, so basalt is kept.

name: Eastern Desert north-east of Qena
note: Top-0.5% area for Jezero in the world scan, in Egypt's Eastern Desert. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Carbonate from ASTER, confirmed by NASA EMIT: carbonate in 100% of 90 mineral detections.

name: Desert south of Al Haruj
note: Top-0.5% area for Jezero in the world scan, south of the Al Haruj lava field. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Carbonate from ASTER, confirmed by NASA EMIT: carbonate in 67% of 99 mineral detections.

name: Ngari plateau
note: Top-0.5% area for Jezero and the lunar pit in the world scan. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 84% of 43 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Ica Desert
note: Top-0.5% area for Jezero in the world scan: hyper-arid coastal desert of southern Peru. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Clay from ASTER; NASA EMIT agrees: clays, with carbonate in only 3% of 112 detections.

name: Moquegua desert
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar pit in the world scan, at the northern end of the Atacama. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds clays and almost no carbonate (1% of 133 detections), so it is scored as clay.

name: Hoh Xil plateau
note: Top-0.5% area for Arcadia outside Antarctica: high, cold plateau with permafrost. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 95% of 37 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Arka Tag highlands
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar pit in the world scan. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 68% of 56 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Qinghai highlands near Hala Lake
note: Top-0.5% area for Arcadia outside Antarctica, east of the studied Qaidam Basin. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 66% of 73 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Eastern Pamir plateau
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar pit in the world scan. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER; NASA EMIT finds carbonate in 93% of 27 mineral detections, so it is scored as carbonate.

name: Arctic Nunavut (Gulf of Boothia coast)
note: Top-0.5% area for Arcadia outside Antarctica: cold polar lowland with permafrost. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Lava Beds National Monument
note: More than 750 lava-tube caves; site of NASA's BRAILLE Mars cave-analog project (rovers and life detection in lava tubes). Added as a documented lava-tube field to test the cave ranking.

name: El Malpais National Monument
note: Large lava tubes (some caves over 1 km) used as a lunar analog since 1970; Big Tubes area of the Zuni-Bandera field. Added as a documented lava-tube field to test the cave ranking.

name: Undara lava tubes
note: One of the longest lava-tube systems on Earth (over 100 km, Bayliss Cave 1.3 km), in tropical savanna. Added as a documented lava-tube field to test the cave ranking.

name: Harrat al-Shaam near Jawa
note: Young pāhoehoe basalt with documented lava tunnels, including Al-Fahda (Khsheifa) Cave, about 920 m long. Added as a documented lava-tube field to test the cave ranking.

name: Payenia lava flows near Puelén
note: Very long pāhoehoe basalt flows with lava tunnels and caves (El Julepe cave, Cueva de Halada) in the Payenia volcanic province. Added as a documented lava-tube field to test the cave ranking.

name: Eastern Karakoram
note: Largest top-0.5% area for the lunar south pole in the world scan: high, glaciated mountains above 5,000 m. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Cumberland Peninsula, Baffin Island
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar south pole in the world scan: steep, glaciated Arctic mountains. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Verkhoyansk Range
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar south pole in the world scan: steep, extremely cold mountains on continuous permafrost. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Saint Elias Mountains
note: Top-0.5% area for the lunar south pole in the world scan: very steep, heavily glaciated mountains. Found by the Earth Engine world scan at 5 km; values here are measured over a 10 km circle. Rock type unclear from ASTER, so it is scored as neutral.

name: Plateau south-east of Kharga Oasis
note: Best 10 km spot for Jezero in a 250 m Earth Engine scan of the Kharga area: flat Eocene limestone plateau about 45 km south-east of the first Kharga site, away from the escarpment. Carbonate from ASTER, confirmed by NASA EMIT at this exact spot: carbonate in 100% of 77 mineral detections.

name: Aksai Chin plateau (eastern part)
note: Best 10 km spot for Jezero in a 250 m Earth Engine scan of the Aksai Chin area (at the box edge). ASTER suggested carbonate, but NASA EMIT finds carbonate in only 11% of 45 detections here (clays 96%), so it is scored as clay: Aksai Chin’s carbonate is patchy.
